arguments.content:
Below are practical, coat-safe steps to bathe and blow-dry a Maltese so the hair stays silky, bright, and as mat-free as possible. Plan on **60–90 minutes total** (longer for a full show-length coat or heavy tangles).

1) **Gather the right products and tools (5–10 min)**  
   - **Shampoo (gentle, moisturizing):** dog-specific, tearless or “sensitive skin” options; whitening/brightening shampoo *only if needed* and not every bath.  
   - **Conditioner:** moisturizing/repair conditioner for long coats; consider a **detangling conditioner**.  
   - **Leave-in coat spray:** detangling/conditioning spray for brushing and drying.  
   - **Tools:**  
     - **Pin brush** (long pins, no ball tips preferred for silky coats)  
     - **Greyhound-style metal comb** (coarse + fine) for line-combing checks  
     - **Slicker brush** (soft to medium) for small tangles (use gently)  
     - **Dematting tool** only for stubborn mats (use sparingly; avoid coat damage)  
     - **Absorbent towels** + optional **microfiber towel**  
     - **High-velocity dryer** (with adjustable speed) and/or **stand dryer**  
     - **Non-slip bath mat**, **cotton balls for ears** (optional), **eye wash** (optional)  

2) **Pre-brush and de-tangle before the bath (10–20 min)**  
   Mist the coat lightly with a **leave-in detangling spray** (never brush a dry Maltese coat). Use **line brushing**: part the hair, brush a small section from skin outward, then follow with the **metal comb** to confirm it’s tangle-free. Remove small knots now—water tightens mats.

3) **Prep the bathing area and protect ears/eyes (2–5 min)**  
   Place a **non-slip mat** in the tub/sink. Use lukewarm water. If desired, place a small cotton ball at each ear opening (don’t push into the canal) to reduce water entry. Keep water and product away from the eyes.

4) **Fully wet the coat (3–5 min)**  
   Saturate from neck to tail, legs, and belly. Maltese coats can repel water at first—take time to wet through to the skin so shampoo distributes evenly.

5) **Shampoo correctly (5–10 min)**  
   Dilute shampoo if recommended (often 1:5 to 1:10) and apply in sections. Massage gently down to the skin without rough scrubbing. Clean the face with a damp cloth and a tiny amount of diluted, tearless shampoo if needed. Rinse thoroughly.

6) **Second shampoo (optional but common for long coats) (3–8 min)**  
   A second wash often improves cleanliness and brightness. If using a **whitening shampoo**, use it as the second wash and follow label timing—don’t overuse to avoid dryness. Rinse extremely well.

7) **Condition deeply and de-tangle in the tub (5–10 min)**  
   Apply conditioner from ears/neck down through ends (avoid heavy product on the scalp if it weighs the coat down). Gently finger-comb or use a wide end of the comb to distribute. Let it sit per label (often 2–5 minutes). Rinse well, leaving only a light slip—not residue.

8) **Towel dry the right way (5–10 min)**  
   Press and squeeze water out with towels—**do not rub** (rubbing causes tangles). Use a microfiber towel to reduce frizz and speed drying. For longer coats, you can “wrap” and blot in sections.

9) **Apply leave-in and begin controlled blow drying (20–40 min)**  
   Mist a **leave-in conditioner/detangler** lightly. Use a **high-velocity dryer** on a controlled setting to push water off the coat (keep airflow moving and avoid blasting one spot). Follow with warm (not hot) airflow to dry to the skin. Keep the nozzle at a safe distance and monitor ear/skin comfort.

10) **Brush/comb while finishing the blow dry (10–20 min)**  
   As you dry, use **line brushing** with the pin brush and check each section with the **metal comb** down to the skin (behind ears, armpits, collar area, groin, and legs are common mat zones). Finish only when the coat is **100% dry**—damp hair mats quickly. Lightly mist detangler as needed.

With a gentle shampoo/conditioner routine, careful towel technique, and line-brushing during drying, a Maltese coat can stay silky and largely tangle-free. Regular upkeep between baths (quick daily comb-through of friction areas) will dramatically reduce mats and make bath day faster.
